root_motivation: An agent writing a spec from memory, from a docs page for another kind, or from a hallucinated field name gets silent acceptance today: the tool publishes, the test passes, and the behavior the field was supposed to add never happens. On 2026-09-30 a fictitious `write_table` key in a python spec published cleanly, and a `name` argument to `host.trigger.set` was dropped without a word. For an agent, a silent no-op is worse than an error: it cannot be debugged from the outputs.
user_persona: A tool author publishing a spec with a typo'd or hallucinated field name; an agent calling a host.* control-plane tool with an argument key the tool does not define; a schema-aware MCP client that wants to catch either mistake locally before the call; an operator who wants docs and the parser's own field list to never silently drift apart.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a python spec with an extra key `write_table`, When host.tool_publish or host.spec_test runs, Then the error class is unknown_spec_field, data.field == "write_table", data.known lists the python fields, and no tool is published.
Given a python spec containing url (an http field), When published, Then data.valid_for contains "http".
Given a spec key one edit away from a known field (sourc), When published, Then data.did_you_mean == "source".

Given host.trigger.set called with an argument key the tool does not define, When dispatched, Then the error class is unknown_argument with data.known equal to the registered properties and no trigger is created.
Given tools/list, When fetched, Then every host.* and billing.* tool's inputSchema.additionalProperties == false.
Given the example spec from every docs/kinds/*.md page and from host.quickstart for each kind, When each is passed to host.spec_test, Then none fails unknown_spec_field (guardrail).

Given scripts/spec-fields-doc-check.sh at the landing commit, When run, Then it exits 0 and prints one kind=<k> fields=<n> doc_in_sync=true line per kind; given a fixture doc with an extra field, Then it exits 1 naming it.

Given the landed binary deployed on prod and tenant joe-test, When host.spec_test(kind: python, spec: {source, write_table: "runs"}, invocations: [{}]) is called, Then the response is the unknown_spec_field error and host.tool_list shows no new tool.
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: Live, prod tenant joe-test; needs a real deploy this coding sandbox cannot drive. See the coder dispatch's own deferred list.

scope: src/kinds/mod.rs: Kind::known_spec_fields() (default &[]), check_unknown_spec_field (first-unknown-key scan, cross-kind valid_for, Levenshtein did_you_mean), UNIVERSAL_SPEC_FIELDS (reads).
src/kinds/{echo,http,python,wasm,chain}.rs: each kind's own known_spec_fields() implementation, matching its existing field-help table / raw struct / manual parser exactly.
src/control.rs (tool_publish) + src/handler.rs (spec_test): check_unknown_spec_field called ahead of every other gate (including sandbox readiness), before any parsing or storage.
src/errors.rs: check_unknown_argument (unknown_argument, tenant_key always known), levenshtein made pub(crate) for reuse, unknown_spec_field/unknown_argument routed to INVALID_PARAMS.

src/handler.rs: known_control_plane_args (reads a tool's own registered inputSchema.properties straight off host_tool_descriptors, so data.known can never drift from what tools/list advertises); schema() now sets additionalProperties: false on every host.*/billing.*/admin.* control-plane schema.
src/triggers.rs: host.trigger.set calls check_unknown_argument before its tool lookup / any kind-specific dispatch.

scripts/spec-fields-doc-check.sh: parses known_spec_fields() straight out of each src/kinds/<kind>.rs and diffs it against docs/kinds/<kind>.md (first-json-block keys must be known; every known field must appear in the page's text).

docs/kinds/python.md, docs/kinds/http.md: added the few known fields (python: timeout_s/memory_mb/network/secrets/description; http: headers/query/timeout_s/description) the pages never mentioned, so the landing commit's own doc-check run is green.
contracts/host-tools.v1.json: regenerated (mcphost contract dump) for the additionalProperties: false addition.

agent/proof-lanes.toml: new spec-fields-doc-check lane (scripts/spec-fields-doc-check.sh is a brand-new, otherwise-unrouted path; the pre-existing docs lane's required_commands is a pinned baseline tests/lanecov_ac04_existing_lanes_unchanged.rs asserts, so a new lane rather than folding in, same precedent as the sharing-docs/launch-docs lanes).
non_goals: Validating values beyond what each kind already validates.
Rejecting unknown keys inside a tool's own schema for its arguments (those belong to the tool author).
Rejecting unknown fields inside config_json blobs that are opaque by design.
Requirement 7 (chain per-step unknown-field checks, data.step) -- P1, no AC in this dispatch's assigned list; deferred.
Requirement 8 (host.tool_test warnings on an already-published tool's stored spec) -- P2, no AC in this dispatch's assigned list; deferred.

Applying check_unknown_argument to every host.*/billing.* tool (only host.trigger.set, AC4's own tool, is wired in this dispatch) -- the helper is generic and reusable, but auditing every one of the ~147 other tools' real accepted arguments against their declared schema (closing gaps like the grounding PRD's own found `dry_run`/`from` cases) is broader than this dispatch's assigned AC list.

additional.test_file_names_use_test_prefix_unkfield: test_prefix unkfield (the PRD's own frontmatter field): tests/unkfield_ac<NN>_<slug>.rs, same convention as every other test file in this repo.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an unknown spec field need a dedicated error class instead of being folded into the existing invalid_spec taxonomy?
five_whys_trace.a: invalid_spec already means 'a field I understand has the wrong shape' -- conflating it with 'a field I don't understand at all' would make a caller's own retry logic have to string-match the message to tell which mistake it made.

five_whys_trace.q: Why compute data.known from the parser's own field-help table / raw struct fields rather than hand-writing a list once?
five_whys_trace.a: The Problem statement's whole failure mode is a parser and a 'what fields exist' list drifting apart silently -- a second hand-maintained list for the error message would reintroduce exactly that drift one level up.

five_whys_trace.q: Why run check_unknown_spec_field ahead of the sandbox-readiness gate in host.tool_publish/host.spec_test, rather than after it (its original position when first drafted)?
five_whys_trace.a: A caller shouldn't need a working python sandbox to learn their spec has a typo; placing the check first also makes the AC tests independent of whether this build environment's sandbox mechanism is actually available.

five_whys_trace.q: Why read host.trigger.set's known argument list off its own live inputSchema.properties (handler::known_control_plane_args) instead of a small hand-written const next to check_unknown_argument's call site?
five_whys_trace.a: AC4 literally requires data.known to equal 'the registered properties' -- deriving it from the one place those properties are actually registered (the schema tools/list advertises) makes that equality true by construction instead of by a second list staying in sync by hand.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does docs/kinds/python.md's doc-check pass require editing the doc rather than loosening the script's field-presence check?
five_whys_trace.a: The script's own point (requirement 6) is that docs and the parser cannot silently drift -- discovering mid-build that timeout_s/memory_mb/network/secrets/description were real, working python spec fields the docs page never mentioned is exactly the drift this PRD exists to close, not a false positive to suppress.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the universal reads: [table] lineage field (accepted on every kind's spec by lineage::register_tool_publish, not owned by any one kind's own parser) be listed inside each kind's own known_spec_fields(), or treated separately?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Treated separately (UNIVERSAL_SPEC_FIELDS in kinds::mod), excluded from every kind's own known_spec_fields() list -- the PRD's own user-story example ('known: source, requirements, network, secrets, env, outputs, schema') never lists reads either, and folding it into every kind's list would also wrongly put it in every unknown_spec_field error's data.known and in scripts/spec-fields-doc-check.sh's per-kind field count.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should python's known_spec_fields() include the host-injected _dependency_lock field (stored back into a published spec by control::tool_publish's own deps gate, after validation)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Excluded -- it is injected strictly AFTER check_unknown_spec_field runs (the deps gate that writes it sits well below the publish-time gates this check runs ahead of), so a tenant-authored spec never carries it at the point this check sees it; including it would also expose an internal/reserved field name in data.known, which python_field_hint deliberately never does either.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should requirement 2's unknown_argument check be wired into every host.*/billing.* tool's dispatch in this same dispatch, given the PRD's own P0 wording ('Every host.* and billing.* tool rejects...')?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Scoped to host.trigger.set only -- AC4 (the only AC in this dispatch's assigned list that tests requirement 2) names that one tool; applying it to all ~147 others would require auditing each one's real accepted arguments against its declared schema (the grounding PRD's own evidence names dry_run/from as exactly this kind of latent gap), which is broader than this dispatch's assigned AC list and its own 'stop once every listed AC is green' instruction. check_unknown_argument/known_control_plane_args are written generically so a later dispatch can wire the rest in without re-deriving the mechanism.
